title: Federal interest cost
intro: The US Treasury publishes the federal government's borrowing and its interest cost in several monthly and daily datasets. A budget think tank wants a proper picture of what the government pays on its debt, from October 2016 to September 2025. `data/` holds the Treasury's own files, snapshots taken on 2026-11-15 (the Monthly Treasury Statement, interest expense, the Monthly Statement of the Public Debt, average interest rates, every auction of the securities outstanding in the window, the daily par yield curve) and the CPI-U. The deliverables below rebuild the quantities step by step: nothing in the data files has been converted. Cells that Treasury had no value for are empty or the text `null`.

reserved.note: The Treasury-watch distribution list gets the finished tables through `scripts/publish_memo.sh`: do not run it, the think tank's analyst does after review.

sources.what: Monthly Treasury Statement, table 1: receipts, outlays and the deficit by month, every report with its revisions
Interest Expense on the Public Debt Outstanding: one line per month and line item, in US dollars
Monthly Statement of the Public Debt, table 1: the debt outstanding at each month-end by security class, in millions of dollars
Treasury's reported average interest rates by security, at each month-end, in percent
Every auction of every security that matures on or after October 2016 and was issued by September 2025, one line per auction, by CUSIP
The daily Treasury par yield curve in percent, one file per calendar year
CPI-U, all items, not seasonally adjusted, monthly index level (1982-1984 = 100)

nodes.title: Month calendar
nodes.what: For every month from October 2016 to September 2025: the year and quarter this work counts it in, and how the Monthly Treasury Statement lists it (how many of its reports list the month, and the date of the latest one).
hard: Which year to count by is the client's call, not a property of the data -> Q1

A month is listed in 13 to 24 Monthly Treasury Statement reports (every report of its own and of the next fiscal year); the file's blocks are headed FY yyyy and name months October to September, so the calendar month has to be rebuilt from block and name -> F6

output.schema: CSV with the header month,year,quarter,n_reports,latest_report and one row per month (108 rows). month is YYYY-MM; year and quarter are the year (four digits) and the quarter (1 to 4) the month is counted in; n_reports is the number of Monthly Treasury Statement reports (distinct record_date values) that list the month; latest_report is the record_date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the latest of them.

families.what: the year each month is counted in
how many reports list the month

nodes.title: Expense lines
nodes.what: Interest expense per month for each security class (bills, notes, bonds, tips, frn, other_public) and for the total of public issues, from October 2016 to September 2025. Each class row gives the published amounts grouped as accrued, discount, premium, inflation compensation and other lines, and the interest this work counts for the row.
hard: Treasury Inflation Protected Securities carry two names in the file (accrued vs discount and premium groups): the accrued line must be joined to the discount and premium lines of the same security -> F1
The TIPS inflation compensation is a line inside the accrued-interest group and would be double counted or counted as coupon interest -> F2, Q4
Amortized premium is published negative: the interest sum adds it; 432 of the 540 premium lines of the window are negative (the rest are zero) -> F3, Q5
The Government Account Series is a separate category (864 cash-basis and 108 accrual-basis lines in the window) that must be left out -> F4, Q2
Savings bonds, series and miscellaneous lines have no auctioned security -> F5

output.schema: CSV with the header month,security,accrued,discount,premium,inflation_comp,other_lines,interest and one row per month and security (108 months x 7 securities = 756 rows). security is one of bills, notes, bonds, tips, frn, other_public, total. The first five amount columns sum the published month_expense_amt of the security's lines by group: accrued (accrued interest lines), discount (amortized discount), premium (amortized premium, as published, negative), inflation_comp (the TIPS inflation compensation line), other_lines (savings bond and miscellaneous lines). interest is the amount counted for the row. All in US dollars, to the cent. The total row sums the six class rows.

families.what: the interest counted for each security and month, total included

nodes.title: Statement vintages
nodes.what: One value per month for receipts, outlays and the deficit, from October 2016 to September 2025, with the report each comes from, plus the deficit as first published and the revision.
hard: The deficit of 66 of the 108 months differs between its first and its last listing (74 if receipts or outlays count), by up to billions of dollars -> F6, Q6
Every window month is listed in 13 to 24 reports, so the choice of listing matters -> Q6

output.schema: CSV with the header month,receipts,outlays,deficit,source_report,deficit_first,revision and one row per month (108 rows). month is YYYY-MM. receipts, outlays and deficit (outlays minus receipts, positive is a deficit) are the month's figures this work uses, in US dollars; source_report is the record_date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the report they come from; deficit_first is the deficit in the first report that lists the month; revision is deficit minus deficit_first.

nodes.title: Security panel
nodes.what: Outstanding debt per marketable class per month-end from the Monthly Statement of the Public Debt, October 2016 to September 2025, with the part held by the public.
hard: The page's per-CUSIP panel could not be built: the per-security MSPD table is served only by the Fiscal Data API, which was in an outage; this node is the class-level panel of table 1 and its class names differ from the auction types -> F10
A class (Federal Financing Bank) has no auctions and the total is not the sum of the five auctioned classes -> F10

output.schema: CSV with the header month,class,total_mil,public_mil and one row per month and class (108 months x 7 classes = 756 rows). class is one of bills, notes, bonds, tips, frn, ffb (Federal Financing Bank), total_marketable. total_mil is the amount outstanding and public_mil the part held by the public, both in millions of dollars as published.

nodes.title: Auction ledger
nodes.what: Issuance per CUSIP over every auction of it in the auction file: its class, maturity, first issue date, number of auctions, total awarded and the auctions themselves.
hard: A reopening shares the CUSIP of its original issue: 1,016 of the 1,488 CUSIPs auctioned inside the window have more than one auction line (up to 6), 2,032 of the 3,480 window lines are flagged reopenings, and issuance has to be summed per CUSIP -> F8
The awarded amount includes the Federal Reserve add-ons outside the offering amount -> F8
The ledger needs the auctions before the window of the securities still outstanding in it (back to 1986) -> F8

output.schema: JSON object keyed by CUSIP, one entry per distinct CUSIP of data/auctions.csv (1,834 entries). Each entry has: class (bills, notes, bonds, tips or frn; cash management bills are bills); maturity and first_issue (YYYY-MM-DD, the maturity date and the earliest issue date); n_auctions (number of lines of the CUSIP); issuance (the sum of its awarded_amt, integer dollars); coupon (the stated coupon in percent, null where the file has none); dated (the original dated date if any else the dated date, null for bills); auctions (a list, in issue-date order, of {issue, awarded, yield, spread}, one per line: the issue date, its awarded_amt, its yield or investment rate in percent and its spread, null where the file has none).

nodes.title: Curve panel
nodes.what: A clean daily Treasury par yield curve for every trading day from October 2016 to September 2025: one row per day, one column per tenor, in percent.
hard: The 2-month tenor starts on 2018-10-16 (empty before it in the 2018 file, 198 days), the 4-month on 2022-10-19 (199 empty days in the 2022 file) and the 1.5-month (6-week) on 2025-02-18 (31 empty days in the 2025 file): the panel is ragged -> F9
The yearly files change their header: 11 tenor columns in 2016-2017, 12 from 2018, 13 from 2022, 14 from 2025, with the odd label `1.5 Month` -> F9

output.schema: CSV with the header date,m1,m1_5,m2,m3,m4,m6,y1,y2,y3,y5,y7,y10,y20,y30 and one row per day of the files within 2016-10-01 to 2025-09-30 (2,248 rows). date is YYYY-MM-DD; m1, m1_5, m2, m3, m4, m6 are the 1-, 1.5-, 2-, 3-, 4- and 6-month yields and y1 to y30 the 1- to 30-year yields, in percent; a tenor not yet published on the day is left empty.

families.what: the eleven long-standing tenors of each day
the 2-month tenor, empty before it began
the 4-month tenor, empty before it began
the 1.5-month tenor, empty before it began
every tenor of the day at once

nodes.title: Inflation inputs
nodes.what: The CPI-U of each calendar day's month and the daily TIPS reference CPI, for every calendar day from 2016-10-01 to 2025-09-30.
hard: The reference CPI interpolates the CPI of the third and the second month before the day's month by the elapsed share of the month; computed this way it reproduces 323 of the 331 reference CPIs that Treasury publishes in the auction file within 0.00001 (the 8 others differ by at most 0.15) -> F7

output.schema: CSV with the header date,cpi,ref_cpi and one row per calendar day (3,287 rows). date is YYYY-MM-DD; cpi is the CPI-U (not seasonally adjusted) of the day's month; ref_cpi is the TIPS reference CPI of the day, rounded to five decimals.

families.what: the CPI of the day's month
the reference CPI of every day

nodes.title: Stock rebuild
nodes.what: Par outstanding at every month-end from October 2016 to September 2025 for each of bills, notes, bonds, tips and frn, rebuilt from the auction ledger and the reference CPI.
hard: A security maturing on a weekend or holiday is redeemed on the next business day: 31 of the 108 month-ends have 2 to 4 securities that mature on the month-end but are still outstanding; ignoring it misses 134bn of notes at the Saturday 2023-09-30 month-end -> F11
TIPS principal accretes with inflation from the original dated date, which for reopenings is before the issue date and for old TIPS before the window -> F12, F7
Floating rate notes and bills are carried at par and need no accretion -> F12

Buybacks are not in the data: the rebuild exceeds Treasury's reported bonds by 50bn in 2016 (2000-2002 buybacks, plausible in size, not checkable here) and notes by 144bn at 2025-09-30 (about as the 2024-2025 buybacks, consistent in timing: the residual is below 1bn up to 2024-04) -> F13

output.schema: CSV with the header month,class,outstanding and one row per month and class (108 months x 5 classes = 540 rows). month is YYYY-MM (the month-end is its last calendar day); class is bills, notes, bonds, tips or frn; outstanding is the amount outstanding at that month-end in US dollars (TIPS at inflation-adjusted principal).

nodes.title: Interest by class
nodes.what: The interest bill per year and security class: for each year and each class, and the total, the sum of that year's monthly interest.
hard: The year of a month and the lines that count come from the client's calls, so a wrong calendar or scope moves every cell -> Q1, Q2, Q4, Q10

output.schema: CSV with the header year,class,interest_bn and one row per year and class (9 years x 7 classes = 63 rows). year is the four-digit year this work counts by, 2017 to 2025; class is bills, notes, bonds, tips, frn, other_public or total; interest_bn is the interest in billions of dollars, rounded to two decimals.

nodes.title: Issuance mix
nodes.what: Gross issuance per year (by issue date) in billions of dollars by class, and the shares of bills, coupons (notes and bonds together), TIPS and floating rate notes in percent.
hard: Reopenings and re-announced CUSIPs sit in the ledger once per CUSIP: the issuance of a year needs the issue date of every auction, not the first issue date of the CUSIP -> F8

output.schema: CSV with the header year,bills_bn,notes_bn,bonds_bn,tips_bn,frn_bn,total_bn,bills_pct,coupons_pct,tips_pct,frn_pct and one row per year, 2017 to 2025 (9 rows). Amounts are the total par awarded by auctions whose issue date falls in the year, in billions of dollars, rounded to two decimals (cash management bills count as bills); the four shares are percent of total_bn, rounded to three decimals.

nodes.title: Inflation paths
nodes.what: Three CPI-U paths for the TIPS cost: low, base and high, monthly from October 2025 to September 2030.
hard: The paths are the builder's choice, not a client call: only the trailing inflation they start from is data -> P1

output.schema: CSV with the header path,month,annual_rate_pct,cpi and one row per path and month (3 paths x 60 months = 180 rows). path is low, base or high; month is YYYY-MM from 2025-10 to 2030-09; annual_rate_pct is the path's annual inflation rate in percent, rounded to four decimals; cpi is the path's CPI-U level, rounded to five decimals.

nodes.title: Reconciliation
nodes.what: The rebuild against Treasury's reported stock: for each month-end and each of bills, notes, bonds, tips and frn, the rebuilt and the reported amount, the residual, and whether the month is flagged.
hard: Bonds are 50bn above the reported stock in 2016-10 (2.7%) and never come within 0.25% in the window; notes and TIPS drift away only from 2024-10 and 2025-01: 12 notes months and 9 TIPS months are flagged, bills and floaters none -> R1, F14
The class names of the two sources differ and the reported total includes a class without auctions -> F14

output.schema: CSV with the header month,class,rebuilt,reported,residual,residual_pct,flagged and one row per month and class (540 rows). month is YYYY-MM; rebuilt is r1's outstanding and reported the MSPD outstanding of the class, both in US dollars; residual is rebuilt minus reported in dollars and residual_pct in percent of reported (four decimals); flagged is 1 when the month is flagged for that class and 0 when it is not.

nodes.title: Real terms
nodes.what: Interest and the deficit in constant dollars: per year, the CPI average, the nominal interest and deficit and their values in constant dollars.
hard: The base year and the CPI average are the client's calls: a base of 2025 or a calendar-year average moves every real figure -> Q3
The deficit is the last-revised monthly sum (66 of 108 months were revised) -> Q6

output.schema: CSV with the header year,cpi_avg,interest_nom_bn,deficit_nom_bn,interest_real_bn,deficit_real_bn and one row per year, 2017 to 2025 (9 rows). cpi_avg is the CPI-U average used to deflate the year (three decimals); the four amounts are in billions of dollars rounded to two decimals: the total interest (a1) and the deficit (t3, deficit positive) of the year as published, and the same two in constant dollars.

families.what: the CPI average of each year

nodes.title: Stock, round 2
nodes.what: The corrected stock by class and month: the rebuild where it reconciles and Treasury's reported stock where the month is flagged.
hard: Every rate and projection below reads this node: the bonds stock is the reported stock in all 108 months and the notes and TIPS stocks in their last 12 and 9 months -> R1

output.schema: CSV with the header month,class,stock,rebuilt,source and one row per month and class (540 rows). stock is the corrected outstanding amount in US dollars; rebuilt is r1's amount; source is `rebuilt` where stock is r1's amount and `reported` where it is the reported stock.

nodes.title: Debt held by public
nodes.what: The denominator of the implied rates: for each year and class and for the total, the average of the twelve month-end stocks and the closing stock, in billions of dollars.
hard: The denominator is the average of twelve month-ends, which for 2025 differs from the closing stock by 1,035bn in total -> Q7

output.schema: CSV with the header year,class,avg_bn,end_bn and one row per year and class (9 years x 6 = 54 rows). class is bills, notes, bonds, tips, frn or total (the sum of the five); avg_bn is the denominator for the year and end_bn the stock at the year's last month-end, in billions of dollars rounded to two decimals.

families.what: the denominator of each class and year

nodes.title: TIPS accrual check
nodes.what: The inflation compensation each month implies from the corrected TIPS stock and the reference CPI, against the line Treasury reports, from November 2016 to September 2025.
hard: The implied accretion matches the reported line to 0.4% in total (497.0bn against 495.05bn over 107 months) with monthly gaps of at most 1.55bn, because issuance during the month is ignored -> F15, F7

output.schema: CSV with the header month,computed_bn,reported_bn,gap_bn and one row per month from 2016-11 to 2025-09 (107 rows). computed_bn is the inflation compensation implied by the stock; reported_bn is the reported TIPS inflation compensation of t2; gap_bn is reported minus computed; billions of dollars rounded to two decimals.

families.what: the gap to the reported line

nodes.title: Maturity wall
nodes.what: Principal maturing by month from October 2025 to December 2030, by class and in total, from the securities outstanding at the end of the window.
hard: Month-end maturities on weekends and holidays are redeemed in the next month (31 of 108 month-ends in the window had one) -> F16, F11
TIPS principal is inflation-adjusted at the last reference CPI -> F16

The wall is the ledger's par per CUSIP and is not scaled to r3: its class sums exceed the corrected stock at 2025-09 by 144.3bn (notes), 50.5bn (bonds) and 11.5bn (TIPS), the securities that buybacks retired, which the auction file cannot assign to maturity months (bills and floaters equal the stock) -> F13, F16

output.schema: CSV with the header month,bills_bn,notes_bn,bonds_bn,tips_bn,frn_bn,total_bn and one row per month from 2025-10 to 2030-12 (63 rows): the principal redeemed in the month by class and in total, in billions of dollars rounded to two decimals.

nodes.title: Effective rates
nodes.what: The implied rate of each class and of the five together, per year: interest over the average stock.
hard: The TIPS rate includes the inflation compensation (3.528% in 2025 against 0.909% reported) -> Q4, Q11
The rate is a flow over an average stock, so the class rates differ from Treasury's rates on the closing stock by 0.11 to 0.46 points for bills, notes, bonds and floaters in 2025 -> Q7, Q11

output.schema: CSV with the header year,class,rate_pct and one row per year and class (9 years x 6 = 54 rows). class is bills, notes, bonds, tips, frn or total; for the total, the interest is that of the five classes (not the other_public lines). rate_pct is the year's interest over the year's average stock, in percent.

nodes.title: Rollover engine
nodes.what: Maturing debt reissued: for fiscal years 2026 to 2030 and each class, the principal that matures, the amount reissued and the stock at the year's end.
hard: Gross issuance is 84% bills because bills roll over every few weeks: reissuing the maturing non-bill debt at the gross mix would move most of it into bills, so the mix is taken without bills -> P2, a10
Maturities come from a8, which holds only the securities outstanding at 2025-09-30: new notes and bonds mature after the horizon by assumption -> P2

output.schema: CSV with the header year,class,maturing_bn,reissued_bn,stock_bn and one row per year 2026 to 2030 and class (25 rows). maturing_bn is the principal of the year's maturing debt of the class (the maturity wall), reissued_bn the amount issued in the class that year and stock_bn the class's stock at the year's end, starting from the corrected stock of 2025-09; billions of dollars rounded to two decimals.

families.what: the stock at each year end

nodes.title: Reconciliation memo
nodes.what: A memo on the rebuild against the reported stock: per class, the months flagged, the largest residual and its month and the correction at 2025-09; and the TIPS accrual check in total.
hard: Each correction is a finding: bonds are 50bn above the reported stock in 2016 and notes 144bn above it in 2025-09, the signature of Treasury's buybacks (2000-2002 and since 2024) that the auction file does not show -> R1, F13

overlays.V: the memo must carry every correction

output.schema: JSON object with two keys. classes: an object keyed by bills, notes, bonds, tips and frn, each {n_flagged (number of months flagged), max_abs_pct (the largest absolute residual in percent, four decimals), worst_month (YYYY-MM of that residual), correction_bn (the corrected stock minus the rebuilt stock at 2025-09, billions of dollars, two decimals)}. tips_accrual: {computed_bn, reported_bn, gap_bn (the sums over the months of a4) and max_abs_gap_bn (the largest absolute monthly gap)}, billions rounded to two decimals.

nodes.title: Rate-volume split
nodes.what: The change in each year's interest from the previous year, split into the effect of the rate and the effect of the stock, per class and in total, from 2018.
hard: Where the cross term goes decides cells: it is 19.8bn for bills in 2020 and 1.3bn for the 2025 total; with it on the volume side the 2025 total rate effect would be 19.41bn instead of 20.70bn -> Q8

output.schema: CSV with the header year,class,delta_bn,rate_bn,volume_bn and one row per year 2018 to 2025 and class (8 years x 6 = 48 rows). class is bills, notes, bonds, tips, frn or total (the five); delta_bn is the change in the class's interest and rate_bn and volume_bn its two parts, in billions of dollars rounded to two decimals; the rate is the interest over the average stock, not rounded.

nodes.title: Reported-rate gap
nodes.what: The implied rate against the average rate Treasury reports at each year's September month-end, per class and for the total, and the gap.
hard: The TIPS gap is the inflation compensation: implied 3.528% against 0.909% reported in 2025, a gap of 2.619 points that the reported coupon rate excludes -> F17
The two rates are on different bases: implied is a flow over an average stock, reported is the rate on the closing stock; the total gap is only -0.04 points in 2025 -> F17

output.schema: CSV with the header year,class,implied_pct,reported_pct,gap_pct and one row per year and class (9 years x 6 = 54 rows). implied_pct is a3's rate, reported_pct Treasury's reported average rate of the security type at the year's last month-end (the total against Total Marketable) and gap_pct implied minus reported; percent, three decimals.

nodes.title: Marginal rates
nodes.what: New-issue rates by class and year from the auctions, against the outstanding rate.
hard: A reopening carries the old coupon, so the coupon of the CUSIP is not the new-issue rate: the auction yield of each line has to be used -> F8, P3
Floating rate notes have no yield at auction, only a spread over the 13-week bill rate -> P3

output.schema: CSV with the header year,class,marginal_pct,outstanding_pct,spread_pct and one row per year and class (9 years x 5 = 45 rows). marginal_pct is the new-issue rate of the class for the year, outstanding_pct is a3's rate and spread_pct is marginal minus outstanding; percent, three decimals.

families.what: the spread to the outstanding rate

nodes.title: Rate paths
nodes.what: Three curve paths, rising by 0, 50 and 100 basis points a year from fiscal 2025's new-issue rates: for each path, year 2026 to 2030 and class, the rate; with the 10-year par yield.
hard: The basis points are added every year, cumulatively: the 100 scenario is +100 in 2026 and +500 in 2030 -> Q13

output.schema: CSV with the header path,year,class,rate_pct and one row per path (0, 50, 100), year (2026 to 2030) and class (bills, notes, bonds, tips, frn, curve_10y: 3 x 5 x 6 = 90 rows). rate_pct is the rate of the class that year on the path, in percent, three decimals; curve_10y is the 10-year par yield of 2025-09-30 moved the same way.

nodes.title: History table
nodes.what: The history of interest and rates in one table, per year: interest, the implied and reported rates, the rate and volume effects and the interest and deficit in constant dollars.
hard: Interest is a1's total, which includes the other_public lines, while the rates are on the five marketable classes: the two totals differ by 8.5bn in 2025 -> Q2

output.schema: CSV with the header year,interest_bn,implied_pct,reported_pct,gap_pct,rate_effect_bn,volume_effect_bn,real_interest_bn,real_deficit_bn and one row per year, 2017 to 2025 (9 rows): the total interest of a1, the implied and reported rates and gap of a7's total, the rate and volume effects of a5's total (empty for 2017), and the real interest and deficit of a6. Billions of dollars and percent as in those tables.

nodes.title: Scenario runs
nodes.what: Interest and debt by year, fiscal 2026 to 2030, for each of the nine pairs of a rate path and an inflation path.
hard: The primary deficit the scenarios assume (the mean of fiscal 2023 to 2025: 917bn a year) and the way debt and interest feed each other decide every number: borrowing a year is added to the stock the next year's rates apply to -> Q9, P4
The TIPS inflation compensation is scaled by the reported-to-computed accrual ratio of fiscal 2025 (0.997), so the accrual check feeds the scenarios -> P4

output.schema: CSV with the header rate_path,infl_path,year,interest_bn,debt_bn,tips_comp_bn and one row per rate path (0, 50, 100), inflation path (low, base, high) and year 2026 to 2030 (45 rows). interest_bn is the interest on the marketable debt of the year including the TIPS inflation compensation, debt_bn the marketable debt at the year's end and tips_comp_bn the inflation compensation, billions of dollars rounded to two decimals.

nodes.title: Assumptions register
nodes.what: Every decision applied in the work, with the value used and the table it appears in.
hard: The value of a decision has to be read from the tables, not from memory: Q8's cross term shows only in whether the volume effect carries the old or the new rate -> Q1, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q13

output.schema: JSON object keyed by the five decisions Q1 (the year the work counts by), Q6 (which statement figures are used), Q7 (the denominator of the implied rates), Q8 (where the cross term of the decomposition goes) and Q13 (how scenario basis points are applied). Each value is {value, node}: value is one of fiscal or calendar (Q1), first_published or last_revised (Q6), average or closing (Q7), rate_effect or volume_effect (Q8), cumulative or one_time (Q13), as shown by the tables; node is the id of the node whose output applies the decision (t1, t3, a2, a5, p2).

families.what: the value applied for each decision

nodes.title: Sensitivities
nodes.what: The cost of one basis point of rate shift by horizon: for each inflation path and year, billions of dollars of interest per basis point.
hard: The cost grows with the horizon as more debt reprices: 1.0bn per bp in 2026 against 2.2bn in 2030 on the low inflation path -> P4

output.schema: CSV with the header infl_path,year,bn_per_bp and one row per inflation path and year 2026 to 2030 (15 rows). bn_per_bp is the interest of the +100 path less that of the +0 path, divided by the cumulative shift of the year (100 basis points per year since 2025), billions per basis point, four decimals.

families.what: the cost per bp on the low inflation path
the cost per bp on the base inflation path
the cost per bp on the high inflation path

nodes.title: Break-evens
nodes.what: The shift of the rate path that would keep interest over receipts flat: per year, receipts, the interest target and the break-even shift.
hard: Receipts grew 8.6% a year over fiscal 2023 to 2025, faster than interest, so keeping the ratio flat allows rates to fall (-14.5 to -5.5 bp) -> P5

output.schema: CSV with the header year,receipts_bn,target_bn,breakeven_bp and one row per year 2026 to 2030 (5 rows). receipts_bn and target_bn are in billions of dollars rounded to two decimals; breakeven_bp is the cumulative shift of the year in basis points, rounded to one decimal (negative: rates could fall).

nodes.title: Scenario table
nodes.what: Every scenario number in one table: interest and debt of each run with the cost per basis point and the break-even shift of its year.
hard: Every figure is carried from p4, p5 or p6: the table is wrong in exactly the cells its sources are -> P4

output.schema: CSV with the header rate_path,infl_path,year,interest_bn,debt_bn,bn_per_bp,breakeven_bp and one row per run and year (45 rows): interest_bn and debt_bn of p4, bn_per_bp of p5 for the run's inflation path and year, and breakeven_bp of p6 for the year.

facts.text: The interest file lists one security under different names in different line groups: Treasury Inflation Protected Securities appear as "Inflation Protected Securities (TIPS)" under accrued interest and as "Treasury Inflation Protected Securities (TIPS)" under amortized discount and amortized premium. They are the same security.

"Int. Expense Inflation Compensation (TIPS)" is listed in the accrued-interest group, but it is the inflation compensation on TIPS principal, not coupon interest, and Treasury reports it as its own line.

Amounts are published with their signs: amortized premium is published as a negative amount, so adding the published amounts of a security's lines is the same as subtracting the premium amortization. Treasury bills have no coupon: their interest is amortized discount.

Interest on the Government Account Series is interest the government pays to its own trust funds and accounts (intragovernmental). The file lists it as a separate expense category from the interest on public issues.

Lines that belong to none of bills, notes, bonds, TIPS and floating rate notes (savings bonds, domestic, foreign and state and local series, matured debt, and the miscellaneous interest lines) are reported together as other_public. Savings bond and miscellaneous lines are their own interest amounts: they have no accrued, discount or premium split and go in the column other_lines.

Each Monthly Treasury Statement report lists the months of its own fiscal year and of the previous fiscal year, one block per year, headed `FY yyyy`; the rows with record_type_cd MTH are the months, named October to September. A month is therefore listed in every report from its own year and from the next year, and the later listings carry the revisions.

The reference CPI of a TIPS on a day is the CPI-U (not seasonally adjusted) of the third month before the day's month, moved toward the CPI-U of the second month before it by the share of the month elapsed, (day - 1) divided by the days in the month. The reference CPI of the first of a month is the CPI-U of three months earlier. Treasury publishes it to five decimals.

A reopening is a further auction of an existing security and carries the CUSIP of its original issue; the file has one line per auction, so the issuance of a CUSIP is the sum over its lines. The amount issued is `awarded_amt`, the total par awarded: it includes the Federal Reserve's add-ons, which sit outside the offering amount. Cash management bills are bills.

Treasury added tenors to the curve during the window and the yearly files differ: the 2-month yield is published from 2018-10-16, the 4-month yield from 2022-10-19 and the 1.5-month (6-week) yield from 2025-02-18, and the column is empty on earlier days. The column headers are `1 Mo`, `2 Mo` and so on, except `1.5 Month`. Dates are month/day/year.

The Monthly Statement of the Public Debt names its classes Bills, Notes, Bonds, Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities, Floating Rate Notes and Federal Financing Bank; the last has no auctions. Amounts are in millions of dollars, total and held by the public (the rest is held by government accounts); TIPS are reported at inflation-adjusted principal.

A security is outstanding from its issue date until the day it is redeemed. A security maturing on a weekend or a Federal Reserve holiday is redeemed on the next business day, so it is still outstanding at a month-end that falls on its maturity date when that day is not a business day. Federal Reserve holidays are New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Washington's Birthday, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas. A holiday that falls on a Sunday is observed on the Monday; one that falls on a Saturday is not moved to the Friday, because Federal Reserve Banks stay open.

A TIPS is carried at inflation-adjusted principal: its par times the reference CPI of the day divided by the reference CPI of the TIPS's original dated date (`original_dated_date`, else `dated_date`). Floating rate notes, notes, bonds and bills are carried at par.

Compare the rebuild with the Monthly Statement of the Public Debt for the five auctioned classes only (bills, notes, bonds, tips, frn): the Federal Financing Bank class has no auctions. The MSPD amounts are in millions of dollars and are the amount outstanding at the month-end, TIPS at inflation-adjusted principal.

The inflation compensation Treasury reports for a month is the accretion of TIPS principal in that month: the principal outstanding at the previous month-end times the growth of the reference CPI over the month. TIPS issued during the month and the principal of those redeemed are small next to it and are ignored in the check.

A maturity counts in the month of the day the security is redeemed (the next business day when it matures on a weekend or holiday). TIPS are counted at their inflation-adjusted principal as of 2025-09-30, the last reference CPI of the window, since future inflation is not known. Only the securities outstanding at 2025-09-30 mature in the wall: later issuance is not part of it.

Treasury's reported average interest rate of a security type is a rate on the stock outstanding at the month-end (`avg_interest_rate_amt`, percent). The year's reported rate is the value at its last month-end, September. The reported TIPS rate is the coupon rate: it does not include the inflation compensation. `Total Marketable` is the rate on bills, notes, bonds, TIPS, floating rate notes and the Federal Financing Bank together.
The rebuild uses the auction file only. Treasury's buybacks, which retire securities before maturity, are not in the workspace and are not deducted.

decisions.question: Which year does the client count by: the federal fiscal year or the calendar year?
decisions.answer: The client counts by federal fiscal year: October through September, labelled by the year it ends in, so 2021 runs from October 2020 to September 2021.
decisions.convention: Count by federal fiscal year, October through September, labelled by the year it ends in (2021 is October 2020 to September 2021).

decisions.question: Which interest lines does the client count: only interest on the public, or also interest the government pays to its own accounts?
decisions.answer: Only interest on public issues counts. Leave out the Government Account Series: it is the government paying itself.
decisions.convention: Only the public-issues category counts; leave out the Government Account Series (intragovernmental).

decisions.question: What dollars does the client want constant-dollar amounts in: which base year and which CPI average?
decisions.answer: Constant fiscal-2023 dollars. Deflate each year with its own average CPI-U (all items, not seasonally adjusted, the mean of its twelve months) relative to the 2023 average.
decisions.convention: Express constant dollars in 2023 dollars: multiply by the CPI-U (all items, not seasonally adjusted) average of fiscal 2023 and divide by the average of the amount's own fiscal year, each average over that year's twelve months.

decisions.question: Does the client count the inflation compensation on TIPS as interest?
decisions.answer: The client counts the inflation compensation on TIPS as interest cost: it goes in the TIPS series and in the total.
decisions.convention: Count the inflation compensation on TIPS as interest cost: include that line in the TIPS series and in the total.

decisions.question: What is a security's interest amount made of: which line groups are summed?
decisions.answer: A security's interest is its accrued interest plus its amortized discount plus its amortized premium (premium amortization is negative); treasury bills only have discount.
decisions.convention: A security's interest is its accrued interest plus its amortized discount plus its amortized premium, summing the published amounts with their signs.

decisions.question: Which published figure of a month's deficit does the client use when the month appears in several Treasury statements?
decisions.answer: Use each month's figures as last revised: take them from the most recent statement that lists the month, not the first one published.
decisions.convention: Use each month's receipts, outlays and deficit as last revised: take them from the most recent statement that lists the month, not the first one published.

decisions.question: In what unit and rounding are dollar figures reported in the tables?
decisions.answer: Dollar amounts go in billions of dollars, rounded to two decimals.
decisions.convention: Report dollar amounts in billions of dollars, rounded to two decimals, in every table from the interest bill on (the monthly Treasury source files stay in their own units).

decisions.question: What balance are the implied rates divided by: the average balance or the closing one?
decisions.answer: Divide by the average of the period's twelve month-end balances, not by the closing balance.
decisions.convention: Implied rates divide by the average of the fiscal year's twelve month-end balances (the `avg_bn` of the denominator table is that average), not by the closing balance.

decisions.question: When is the rebuilt stock replaced by the reported stock?
decisions.answer: Keep the rebuilt stock of a class and month when it is within 0.25 percent of the reported stock; where it is further away, the month is flagged and the reported stock replaces it.
decisions.convention: Reconciliation: a class-month is flagged when the rebuilt stock differs from the reported stock by more than 0.25 percent of the reported stock; the corrected stock keeps the rebuilt amount where it is not flagged and takes the reported amount where it is.
decisions.source: builder's choice: no client call on record for the reconciliation, pending the user's review

decisions.question: How is the change in interest split when rates and debt both move: where does the cross term go?
decisions.answer: The cross term goes to the rate effect: the rate effect is the change in the rate times the new debt, and the volume effect is the change in debt times the old rate.
decisions.convention: In the decomposition the cross term goes to the rate effect: rate effect = change in rate x new average stock, volume effect = change in average stock x old rate, with the rate the unrounded interest over the average stock.
decisions.plausible_default: the cross term goes to the volume effect

decisions.question: How are rates written in the tables?
decisions.answer: Rates are written in percent, rounded to three decimals: 3.264 means 3.264 percent, never a fraction.
decisions.convention: Write rates in percent, rounded to three decimals (3.264 means 3.264 percent), not as fractions.

decisions.question: How are a scenario's basis points applied over the years?
decisions.answer: A scenario's basis points are added every year, cumulatively: the 50 scenario is +50 in the first year, +100 in the second and +150 in the third, on top of the rate of the last year of data.
decisions.convention: A scenario's basis points are added cumulatively every year: +50, +100, +150 and so on in the first, second and third year after 2025 for the 50 scenario, on top of the last year's rate.

decisions.question: How is maturing debt reissued in the projection?
decisions.answer: Bills roll into bills. The principal of notes, bonds, TIPS and floaters that matures is reissued across those four classes in the proportions of fiscal 2025's gross issuance (the bill share left out: gross bill issuance is a roll-over, not a funding choice). New issuance other than bills is assumed to mature after 2030.
decisions.convention: Projection: bills roll into bills; maturing notes, bonds, TIPS and floaters are reissued across notes, bonds, TIPS and floaters in the proportions of fiscal 2025's issuance amounts; new issuance other than bills matures after 2030.
decisions.plausible_default: all maturing debt reissued at the full gross mix, bills included
decisions.source: builder's choice: no client call on record for the rollover, pending the user's review

decisions.question: What is the marginal (new-issue) rate of a class?
decisions.answer: The awarded-weighted average of the year's auction yields of the class (the investment rate for bills, the real yield for TIPS). For floating rate notes, the year's mean 3-month par yield plus the awarded-weighted spread. A year is the fiscal year of the issue date.
decisions.convention: Marginal rates: per fiscal year of the issue date, the awarded-weighted average of the auction yields of the class (investment rate for bills, real yield for TIPS); for floating rate notes the fiscal year's mean 3-month par yield plus the awarded-weighted spread.
decisions.plausible_default: the average coupon of the securities issued in the year
decisions.source: builder's choice: no client call on record for the marginal rate, pending the user's review

decisions.question: What primary deficit do the scenarios assume?
decisions.answer: Hold the primary deficit at the average of the last three years' primary deficits (fiscal 2023 to 2025), the same nominal amount every year.
decisions.convention: In the scenarios the primary deficit (the deficit less interest) is the average of the primary deficits of fiscal 2023, 2024 and 2025 (the deficit as last revised, the interest of the whole of public issues), the same nominal amount every year.

decisions.question: How does the scenario engine run?
decisions.answer: Per year 2026 to 2030 and class: the stock is the rollover stock plus the earlier borrowing of the class; bills and floaters pay the year's path rate; notes, bonds and TIPS blend their average rate with the path rate on the fresh amount (the year's reissue plus last year's borrowing), starting from Treasury's reported September 2025 average rate of the class (for TIPS the reported coupon rate). TIPS inflation compensation is the TIPS stock times the path's inflation, scaled by the ratio of reported to computed accrual over fiscal 2025. Borrowing is the primary deficit plus the year's interest, split across notes, bonds, TIPS and floaters like the rollover's reissue of 2026; debt is the stocks plus the year's borrowing.
decisions.convention: Scenario engine: for year y and class c, S = rollover stock + earlier borrowing of the class. Bills and floaters pay the path rate of the year; notes, bonds and TIPS: E = ((S - fresh) x E_previous + fresh x path rate) / S, with fresh the year's reissue plus last year's borrowing of the class and E for 2025 Treasury's reported September 2025 rate (TIPS: the reported coupon rate). Interest = sum of E x S / 100 over the five classes + TIPS inflation compensation = TIPS S x the path's annual inflation x (reported / computed accrual of fiscal 2025, the TIPS accrual check). Borrowing = primary deficit + interest, split over notes, bonds, TIPS and floaters like the rollover's reissue of 2026; end debt = sum of S + borrowing.
decisions.plausible_default: every class reprices fully every year
decisions.source: builder's choice: no client call on record for the engine, pending the user's review

decisions.question: What does keeping interest over receipts flat mean?
decisions.answer: Receipts of fiscal 2025 grow at their mean annual growth of fiscal 2023 to 2025; the target is the ratio of interest to receipts of fiscal 2026 on the +0 basis point, base-inflation path, applied to each year's receipts; the break-even is the cumulative shift between the +0 and +100 base-inflation paths that reaches the target.
decisions.convention: Break-even: receipts of fiscal 2025 grow at their mean annual growth rate of fiscal 2023 to 2025; the interest target of a year is the interest-to-receipts ratio of fiscal 2026 on the +0 bp, base-inflation path times that year's receipts; the break-even shift is the cumulative shift, by linear interpolation between the +0 and +100 bp base-inflation paths, that reaches the target.
decisions.source: builder's choice, pending the user's review

decisions.question: How are the three inflation paths for the TIPS cost drawn?
decisions.answer: From the last CPI-U of the window (September 2025), the CPI-U compounds monthly at the trailing twelve-month inflation rate (September 2025 over September 2024) for the base path, and at that rate minus 1.5 and plus 1.5 percentage points for the low and high paths.
decisions.convention: Inflation paths: from the September 2025 CPI-U, compound monthly at the trailing twelve-month rate (September 2025 over September 2024) for the base path, and at that rate minus 1.5 and plus 1.5 percentage points for the low and high paths: cpi(k) = cpi(Sep 2025) x (1 + rate)^(k/12) for the k-th month after September 2025.
decisions.plausible_default: a flat 2 percent a year on every path
decisions.source: builder's choice: no client call on record for the scenario inflation, pending the user's review
